defects.title: Stale queued prompt leaves authenticated worker idle
defects.description: A stale ServerPrompt could leave the authenticated worker idle while presence heartbeats continued. Iteration 27 traced the recurrence to empty heartbeat prompts being filled from the terminal buffer and heartbeat timestamps being mistaken for prompt-observation timestamps.
defects.root_cause: GameAgentRuntime.NormalizeEvent synthesized an empty heartbeat prompt from the terminal buffer. The worker also fell back to the heartbeat event timestamp when promptObservedAt was absent, and MTC prompt waiters compared heartbeat timestamps instead of the original observation time. A stale screen prompt could therefore appear fresh, while a genuine current prompt could be rejected as old.
fixes_applied: Cache the latest prompt surface in MTC and clear it on client input, non-prompt server output, connect, and disconnect.
Include the still-current prompt surface in presence heartbeats.
Do not synthesize heartbeat prompt surfaces from terminal-buffer contents; carry promptObservedAt and an explicit promptIsCurrent confirmation.
Re-queue heartbeat prompts only when their original observation is fresh or MTC explicitly confirms the cached prompt is still current.
Normalize prompt timestamps before MTC command-sender freshness and in-flight prompt checks.
validation_results: Added a regression test that proves a stale queued Command prompt is recovered from a fresh prompt-bearing heartbeat.

defects.title: Pilot schema offers Dock Shopper when readiness is false
defects.description: During uncounted attempt 24-01, the Pilot repeatedly selected RunStarDockShopper while the ship was in sector 933, not verified StarDock sector 551, and the worker reported missing prerequisites. The deterministic worker rejected the action, so the session made no progress.
defects.root_cause: The structured action schema listed RunStarDockShopper unconditionally; the prompt and downstream validator carried the readiness constraints, but the model could still select the unavailable action.
fixes_applied: Exclude RunStarDockShopper from the schema unless game actions are enabled, readiness is verified, the action has not already been attempted at this sector, and the shopper stage is inactive.
validation_results: Added schema assertions for unavailable and verified-ready Dock Shopper states.
Focused action-provider tests passed: 25 passed, 0 failed; full TradeWars suite passed: 252 passed, 0 failed.
Live validation remains pending; attempt 24-01 was stopped before any movement, trade, or scan.
notes: This was an uncounted stalled attempt, not a productive iteration.
Keep worker-side prerequisite validation fail-closed even with the dynamic schema.

defects.title: Stale trading objective caused scannerless route oscillation
defects.description: While the ship lacked a Density or Holo Scanner, stale/funding trade objectives have repeatedly competed with scanner-first routing. Earlier movement oscillated between sectors 933 and 556; iterations 28 and 29 showed movement between StarDock sector 551 and known high-risk sector 99. Iteration 31 moved 551→172→551 after the Pilot misread the port profile. Iterations 32 and 34 again moved through sectors 172, 206, and 805 without a verified trade or scanner purchase; the exact opportunity and hold-guard inputs were not retained.
defects.root_cause: Persistent map exploration alone is insufficient to make a scannerless route useful or safe, and the Pilot may misread a port's buy/sell profile as a compatible trade. Iterations 31, 32, and 34 show repeated unproductive routes after reaching or approaching StarDock. Iterations 32 and 34 also exposed separate port-recovery defects that explain declined quotes but do not explain the route oscillation. The exact opportunity and hold-guard state during the departures were not captured.
affected_components: Port-trade route selection and scannerless movement safety
fixes_applied: Override stale non-FedSpace trading objectives with a scanner-first StarDock objective when scanner absence and StarDock location are verified.
Constrain movement to the next verified adjacent hop on the known shortest route to StarDock.

When FedSpace is Complete or Skipped and no Density Scanner is owned, keep scanner acquisition as the objective at StarDock despite a stale trading objective; permit only compatible port-pair trades for funding.
Before sending a movement command, block scannerless entry outside sectors 1-10 and StarDock unless the target is recorded as explored.
Block scannerless entry into sector 99 regardless of its persistent Explored flag.

Filter scannerless adjacent movement candidates to sectors 1-10, StarDock, or already-explored sectors before building the Pilot context; suppress remote port-trade opportunities whose next hop is unsafe, while retaining the final execution guard.

At StarDock, hold when the scanner is absent, the Dock Shopper is not ready, the ship has no cargo, and no verified compatible trade opportunity exists, regardless of the current credit balance; do not act on a model-invented trade rationale.
Accept a single-commodity complementary port profile and search for fresh directed trade pairs up to three hops apart outside FedSpace, while retaining scannerless movement guards.
Use the full prompted quantity for the selected, verified product and reject scannerless pair plans whose route to the seller or buyer crosses any uncharted or otherwise disallowed sector.
validation_results: Added RoutesScannerlessShipTowardStarDockDespiteStaleTradingObjective regression coverage.
Focused regression passed; full TradeWars suite passed 254/254 with serialized xUnit execution, then 255/255 after prompt-freshness changes.
Live runtime moved from sector 933 to 805, breaking the previously observed 933/556 oscillation; StarDock arrival and scanner acquisition were not verified.
Added KeepsScannerAcquisitionObjectiveAtStarDockDespiteStaleTradingObjective coverage; both scanner-routing tests passed and the full TradeWars suite passed 256/256.

Iteration 25's updated Release binary reached known StarDock sector 551 from sector 172. It later proposed returning to the known port in sector 172 to fund the scanner, but no fresh post-move state, trade, or scanner purchase was verified.

Iteration 28 loaded the updated Release build and recorded verified sector snapshots at 551, 99, and 551 while the ship had 1 credit and no scanner. The session was stopped before the 15-minute window to avoid further unscanned movement into known dangerous sector 99. No trade or scanner purchase was verified.

Uncounted attempt 29: the Release runtime selected sector 172, which the MTC map identified as uncharted. With no verified scanner, the worker reported that movement was blocked; the verified sector remained 551 and no trade, scan, or scanner purchase occurred. Focused AutonomousTestWorkerTests passed 65/65 and the Release win-x64 build succeeded with 0 warnings and 0 errors.

Iteration 29: after a successful port/warp CIM refresh, the live monitor recorded sectors 551, 99, and 551. Meridian was stopped immediately after the high-risk sector appeared. Added an unconditional scannerless sector-99 block and a regression test; all 67 AutonomousTestWorkerTests passed. The MTC Release build succeeded and was subsequently live-restarted.

Iteration 30: the rebuilt runtime selected a scanner-funding target and recorded movement through sector 206, then failed on an echoed MoveSector prompt. Added a sender regression fix and harness coverage. In a separate uncounted restart, the Pilot proposed unexplored sector 172 without a verified scanner; the worker blocked movement and the ship remained at StarDock 551. A subsequent source repair filters unsafe scannerless routes before Pilot selection; all 68 AutonomousTestWorkerTests passed.

Iteration 31: the published runtime moved 551 to 172 and back to 551 without trading; the Pilot misread the known sector's Fuel Ore-selling port. A later CIM refresh completed, but the read-only Pair Port Trade plan still reported no complementary pair. Added a StarDock hold for the verified no-funds/no-cargo/no-scanner state. All 69 AutonomousTestWorkerTests passed; the published runtime then recorded a hold at StarDock 551. Scanner purchase and WorldTrade remain outstanding.

Pre-cycle-32 safety follow-up: widened the StarDock no-progress hold so any credit balance is held when there is no scanner, no cargo, no ready Dock Shopper, and no verified funding trade. The regression test now exercises 500 credits and passes. The fix is source-tested only; do not treat it as live-validated.

Uncounted source/test follow-up: the macro rejected a valid one-product profile and the general runtime provider searched only direct seller-to-buyer warps. Updated both; all 16 MacroExecutionTests passed and the MTC RPC safety harness passed, including a fresh three-hop non-FedSpace pair. The changes were not loaded into the live MTC, so live funding behavior and scanner acquisition remain unverified.

Source follow-up after the operator reported turns/movement with no earnings and credits reduced to 1: scannerless multi-hop trade plans could traverse unexplored sectors. Routes were filtered against scannerless movement policy. MacroExecutionTests passed 16/16; all 138 MTC RPC safety/dashboard checks passed; Release win-x64 build passed with 0 warnings and 0 errors. No MTC process was running; output was built to a session directory, not deployed. No gameplay progress was claimed.

Iteration 32 completed the full 900-second window and recorded 159 sector changes, including repeated 172↔206 movement, but no verified transaction, cargo, credits, scanner, or WorldTrade progress. The exact route opportunity and guard state were not retained; do not attribute the loop to a specific provider result.

Iteration 34 recorded 168 sector transitions among 172, 206, and 805 with no scanner, trade, or WorldTrade progress. The run again confirms the route-loop symptom but does not identify the opportunity or hold decision that caused it.

Source review after iteration 32 found that any non-null current or remote portTradeOpportunity suppresses the StarDock hold. The run did not retain the opportunity payload, so this is not confirmed as the reason for the observed departure; capture that state before changing route arbitration.
The post-run recovery repair passes verified synchronized credits through untracked trade recovery. Its focused tests pass, but the live runtime has not yet loaded the repair.
notes: Keep this defect REGRESSED until the connected runtime blocks sector 99 without a verified scanner and the objective produces a safe funding route and scanner purchase. The uncounted follow-up blocked a proposed scannerless move to unexplored sector 172, but no safe funding route was selected.

The planner now hides unsafe scannerless routes from the Pilot as well as blocking execution. A live StarDock hold was observed for the one-credit/no-cargo state, but keep the broader defect REGRESSED until scanner acquisition succeeds and sector 99 is verified blocked.
Correlate the funding objective, selected adjacent target, MTC command submission/acknowledgment, and resulting sector snapshot before changing route arbitration.
Do not treat an explored sector as a trade opportunity; require provider-verified port compatibility and adequate ship state before leaving StarDock.

The one-product and three-hop source fixes are not runtime-validated. MTC auto-starts Meridian after restart, so verify and stop the worker safely before replacing the running process or attempting a live check.

The 500-credit StarDock hold test passes in source, but the runtime has not been restarted with this build. Confirm a fresh game snapshot and verified trade opportunity before enabling any game action.

Port prompts expose a maximum quantity, not proof of affordability or profit. Use verified credits during untracked recovery and verify a scannerless route end to end before buying cargo; live stock, cash, and a positive sell-side credit delta still require post-trade verification.

Iteration 32's and 34's lack of a current/remote opportunity record prevents confirming why the StarDock hold did not activate. Capture current sector, TradeSector, RouteSector, product, opportunity freshness, and hold decision inputs before changing route arbitration.

defects.title: Movement sender treats echoed MoveSector prompt as fatal
defects.description: After the MTC sender submitted a movement destination, the terminal surfaced `To which Sector [551] ? 860` before the resulting command prompt. The sender treated this expected echoed MoveSector surface as an unexpected prompt and failed the action before it could observe the fresh movement result.
defects.root_cause: PreventMultiHopMovementAsync handled AutopilotConfirmation, StopInSector, and Command after destination submission, but omitted MoveSector. A destination-echo observation therefore threw immediately instead of waiting for the subsequent result prompt.
fixes_applied: Ignore a post-submission MoveSector echo while waiting for the next fresh movement result prompt.
Add an RPC safety harness case covering a MoveSector echo followed by a fresh Command prompt.
validation_results: MTC RPC safety harness passed 134 checks, including the MoveSector echo regression case.
Release win-x64 MTC publish succeeded.
Live validation remains pending; the next runtime retry stalled before another movement.
notes: The sender only waits through the prompt and does not submit additional input; if no fresh result prompt arrives, the existing timeout remains fail-closed.

defects.title: Pilot pairs a non-movement action with a target sector
defects.description: Pilot responses have paired non-movement actions with nonzero target sectors. The action provider rejected each malformed decision, so none was executed; repeated retries delay autonomous progress.
defects.root_cause: The original schema exposed the union of movement and non-movement target-sector values without encoding their action dependency. The model could pair a valid adjacent sector with a non-movement action, which the parser rejected after generation.
fixes_applied: Add mutually exclusive oneOf schema branches: MoveToAdjacentSector requires a verified adjacent target; all other actions require targetSector=0.
Retain the deterministic parser rejection and add regression assertions for both schema branches.
validation_results: Iteration 24 live Pilot history recorded a non-movement action with targetSector=551; the provider rejected it rather than executing it.
Iteration 25 recorded four additional non-movement/target-sector mismatches; all were rejected before execution.
Focused provider and routing tests passed 4/4; full TradeWars suite passed 256/256.
Local Ollama accepted a oneOf schema smoke test. Live validation of the provider's full oneOf schema is pending.
notes: Do not coerce malformed output into a successful action. Verify the oneOf constraint under live Qwen inference before closing the defect.

defects.title: Stale ship snapshot blocks progress at StarDock
defects.description: During iteration 26, Meridian remained authenticated at Command in sector 551 but the verified ship snapshot stayed stale at 65,440 turns. The last decision remained RequestShipInformation and no fresh status response or further gameplay progress was observed.
defects.root_cause: Unconfirmed. The available dashboard and metric samples do not correlate the server's Command prompt timestamp, the submitted ship-information and quick-status inputs, their acknowledgments, and a fresh snapshot event.
fixes_applied: Filter Pilot context catalog entries to references explicitly exposed as approved script capabilities, rather than forwarding all unreviewed script filenames.
Exclude RequestShipInformation from the Pilot action enum while synchronization and the ship snapshot are healthy and the snapshot is at most 30 seconds old.
validation_results: Iteration 26 remained at sector 551 with a stale snapshot through the end of the 451.1-second sampled worker window.
The terminal remained connected and authenticated at Command, while the dashboard reported no active TWX interpreter scripts.

An uncounted post-build attempt remained at sector 551 with 1 credit and no scanner; the monitor continued to report RequestShipInformation despite healthy synchronization. The worker was stopped after no verified game action.

The Pilot catalog filter is covered by the provider test class (27/27 passed), and the Release win-x64 build passed. Its effect on live inference latency and movement execution is still being observed.

The follow-up worker ran for roughly 15 minutes. At 5:41 PM, the monitor showed a healthy authenticated Command session with a current snapshot at sector 551, 65,330 turns, 1 credit, and no Holo Scanner; the latest decision remained RequestShipInformation. Pilot history showed 44 interactions, Strategic Review 2, and Reflex 94, including two empty-output token-limit failures that each retried. No movement, trade, scan, scanner purchase, or WorldTrade start was verified. Meridian was stopped at 5:43 PM; this attempt is uncounted.
Filtered RequestShipInformation from the Pilot enum for healthy snapshots no older than 30 seconds. All 27 AutonomousTestActionProviderTests passed and the Release win-x64 build passed.

The updated Release build was live-exercised: the monitor recorded movement decisions and verified sector changes. However, the ship oscillated between sectors 551 and 99 without a scanner, so the status-action gate did not solve the overall routing failure.

Uncounted attempt 29: after MTC restart, the authenticated Command snapshot at sector 551 aged stale and no new Pilot LLM call was recorded (Pilot 0, Strategic Review 1, Reflex 5). Meridian was stopped without game progress; the terminal remained connected.
notes: Keep command guards fail-closed. Capture timestamped server prompts, submitted input, RPC acknowledgments, and synchronized snapshot events before changing refresh behavior. A model movement decision alone is not proof that the MTC command was sent or that the postcondition occurred.

The latest run showed a fresh healthy snapshot while the selected action was still RequestShipInformation. After Meridian stopped, the snapshot naturally aged past the 30-second freshness limit. The precise reason no movement or trade was selected remains unconfirmed.

The provider now removes RequestShipInformation from the action enum for a healthy snapshot no older than 30 seconds. This prevents a repeated status no-op when the model obeys the schema, but a fresh route and actual movement still need live verification.

Uncounted attempt 29 restarted MTC with the terminal connected and Meridian running. The monitor later showed a stale snapshot at sector 551; Pilot history contained no calls, while Strategic Review and Reflex showed 1 and 5 interactions. The agent was stopped without gameplay progress. Correlate fresh prompt timestamps, ship-status requests, and acknowledgments before changing refresh behavior.

defects.title: Repeated Fuel Ore haggles do not produce a verified trade
defects.description: The autonomous agent repeatedly selected port products but did not complete a verifiable trade. Iteration 35 verified one full-hold Fuel Ore purchase, but its next sale quote remained unanswered; iteration 36 left two purchase quotes unresolved; iteration 37 selected 20 Fuel Ore holds three times but left affordable 153-, 215-, and 153-credit quotes unanswered. Iteration 38 verified nine transactions and positive earnings, but one interrupted Organics purchase lost its selected product and credit context and was declined with 0. Iteration 39 made verified trades but a later delayed recovery again lost the selected product and credits, declined a 209-credit quote, and submitted 0 at a later quantity prompt. Iteration 40 live-validated recovery context retention with an accepted Fuel Ore sale and fresh cargo/credit verification.
defects.root_cause: The original 5-second quantity-to-offer correlation window was too short and was widened to 45 seconds. Iteration 37 exposed a second prompt-ordering defect: confirmed presence heartbeats were promoted to new actionable prompt timestamps. Filtering those copies enabled live trades in iteration 38. The worker then stored the active selected opportunity before SendAsync, but cleared it as soon as the sender returned rather than retaining it until fresh ship-snapshot verification. A delayed untracked prompt therefore still lacked the original selected product and synchronized credits and could submit 0.
fixes_applied: Use the full prompted hold capacity for the selected, verified product instead of limiting buys to one unit.
Pass the fresh synchronized credit balance into the sender and decline purchase quotes that are not affordable.
Fail closed when multiple port-trade prompts arrive before a response, and stop if native haggling becomes enabled during the trade.
Propagate a valid synchronized credit balance into untracked port-trade recovery and accept quotes that exactly equal the available balance.
Correlate an untracked active quote with its fresh preceding quantity prompt and preserve the selected product/sale context.
Leave an uncorrelated quote unanswered instead of sending 0, and schedule fresh ship-snapshot verification after a recovered opportunity.
Classify `Your offer [amount] ?` as a distinct prompt surface.
Allow a fresh correlated offer to be handled despite a stale Command-prompt indicator.
Extend quantity-to-offer correlation to the 45-second fresh-prompt limit without relaxing the offer, freshness, affordability, approval, or native-haggle checks.
Exclude presence-heartbeat copies from actionable trade-prompt recovery and pending-prompt sequencing; correlate only against actual server prompt text.
Store the active selected trade and starting snapshot before awaiting the sender, then pass the original product, sale/buy intent, follow-up product, and credits through untracked recovery.
Retain the active trade context after SendAsync returns until a fresh snapshot verifies the transaction or the bounded recovery-context age expires.
validation_results: Iteration 26 recorded nine no-transaction Fuel Ore haggle outcomes at sector 172; each retained 17 credits and 20 empty holds.

Iteration 27's 12-hold Fuel Ore quote was 58 credits against 55 available, so no purchase was verified. A later quantity prompt stalled; prompt-timestamp recovery was repaired under DEFECT-0016, but a completed trade is still unverified.
No completed port transaction, scanner purchase, or WorldTrade start was verified.

Iteration 32 recorded three trade attempts and no transaction; the live window ended with 500 credits and 20 empty holds. Source tracing found untracked recovery always passed null credits to quote affordability.

After iteration 32, the worker and MTC recovery interfaces were updated to propagate the fresh balance. All 71 AutonomousTestWorkerTests passed and the MTC RPC safety/dashboard harness passed 149 checks, including a maximum-quantity purchase at an exact-balance quote. The fix had not yet been deployed for live validation.
Iteration 33's available handoff records a 161-credit Fuel Ore quote answered with 0; raw logs and duration were unavailable.

Iteration 34's timestamped debug log confirmed three recovery quotes: 107 and 191 against 500 credits were declined because selection was lost; 140 was declined with credits unknown. Credits remained 500 and all holds remained empty.

Added sender harness coverage for accepting a correlated affordable quote and refusing an unmatched quote without input; all 151 MTC safety/dashboard checks passed. Added worker coverage for fresh-snapshot verification; all 274 TradeWars tests passed. Release build passed with 0 warnings and 0 errors. The repairs required live validation in iteration 35.

Iteration 35 accepted a 191-credit recovered quote against 500 credits. A fresh snapshot verified 20 Fuel Ore and 309 credits, and the ship moved to sector 290. A subsequent sale quote of 876 credits remained unanswered at shutdown.

After iteration 35, added quote-prompt classification and a regression harness case where the command-prompt indicator is stale. The full TradeWars suite passed 276/276, the MTC harness passed 151 checks, and the Release build passed with 0 warnings and 0 errors. This source fix still requires live validation.

The first two iteration-35 recovery attempts did not produce a recorded quote decision. The available logs do not identify their failure branch; keep this defect open until a sale and positive earnings are verified.

Iteration 36 began with 309 credits and 20 empty holds, moved from sector 290 to 805, and made two 20-hold Fuel Ore purchase attempts. Neither offer was accepted or verified; no earnings, scanner purchase, or WorldTrade start occurred.
Iteration 36's first recovery began 8.145 seconds after the quantity prompt, beyond the 5-second correlation limit. Extended the limit to 45 seconds and added a 35-second correlation regression case.
The MTC RPC safety/dashboard harness passed 151 checks and the Release build passed with 0 warnings and 0 errors. These source changes were built after iteration 36 and still need live validation.

Iteration 37 began in sector 805 with 309 credits and 20 empty holds. Three 20-hold Fuel Ore offers (153, 215, and 153 credits) were affordable but unanswered; no cargo or credit delta, scanner purchase, or WorldTrade start was verified.

Iteration 37's event archive shows a confirmed presence heartbeat repeating the PortTradeOffer surface after the actual quote. Heartbeat copies could be mistaken for actionable prompts and interfere with quote correlation.

After iteration 37, filtered heartbeat copies from trade recovery and pending-prompt handling. The MTC safety/dashboard harness passed 151 checks and the Release build passed with 0 warnings and 0 errors; iteration 38 must live-validate the fix.

Iteration 38 live-validated heartbeat filtering: nine transactions raised credits from 309 to 4,072 and the ship reached StarDock with 20 Fuel Ore. One Organics purchase still lost its selected product and 1,010-credit balance during untracked recovery and submitted 0.

After iteration 38, the worker persisted the selected opportunity and starting snapshot before SendAsync, and recovery passed the original product, sale/buy intent, follow-up product, and credits. The worker test class passed 72/72, the MTC harness passed 152 checks, and the Release build passed with 0 warnings and 0 errors. Full-suite status was 275/276 due to a temporary SQLite file-lock cleanup failure; the isolated failing test passed.

Iteration 39 verified a 20-unit Fuel Ore purchase and sale, but a later delayed recovery lost context after SendAsync returned, declined a 209-credit quote, and sent 0 at a later Organics quantity prompt. The active context is now retained until verification or bounded expiry. The delayed-prompt regression and all 73 AutonomousTestWorkerTests passed; the full TradeWars suite passed 277/277; the MTC harness passed 152 checks; and the Release build had 0 warnings and 0 errors.

Iteration 40 live-validated the repair. At StarDock the delayed untracked sale recovery preserved FuelOre, sellingExistingCargo=true, and the 5,555-credit starting balance; it accepted a 966-credit sale. A fresh snapshot then showed credits=6,521, 20 empty holds, and sector 551. The 15-minute window remained connected and ended within 0.019 seconds of target. No scanner purchase or WorldTrade start occurred; those remain separate objectives.
notes: Iteration 34 traced the selection loss through the recovery quote decision; instrument the direct abort branch if the live repair still hands off unexpectedly.
Require a live sale or other positive earnings and a fresh snapshot that verifies cargo and credit deltas before this defect can be marked VALIDATED.
The second iteration-36 recovery attempt remained unresolved despite being within the widened correlation interval; retain branch-level tracing and verify the next live attempt.

Iteration 38 live-validated heartbeat filtering but exposed a separate trade-intent handoff failure. Iteration 39 showed that pre-send context alone is insufficient if it is cleared before a fresh snapshot verifies the transaction. Iteration 40 live-validated retaining context through verification and a completed profitable sale. Scanner acquisition and WorldTrade are not covered by this defect and remain unverified.

defects.title: Pilot oneOf branches omit required shared response fields
defects.description: Movement and non-movement structured-output branches constrained action and targetSector but omitted the root-required rationale and citation fields. Ollama could therefore return branch-valid JSON that failed Pilot validation because rationale was missing, preventing the decision from being used.
defects.root_cause: The oneOf branches were built with only action-specific properties, while rationale, citedKnowledgeNodeId, and conditional scriptInputResponse were declared only at the root. The provider follows the selected branch contract and did not reliably include root-only fields.
fixes_applied: Include rationale and citedKnowledgeNodeId in both oneOf branches and require them at branch level.
Require a non-empty rationale and include scriptInputResponse in each branch only when an approved script prompt is present.
validation_results: AutonomousTestActionProviderTests passed 27/27, including assertions for branch-level required fields, non-empty rationale, and conditional scriptInputResponse.
Release win-x64 LLM Control Center build succeeded with 0 warnings and 0 errors.
After deployment, the live Pilot produced a complete structured MoveToAdjacentSector response with targetSector, rationale, and citedKnowledgeNodeId. No game movement or postcondition was verified.
notes: A valid Pilot response validates the model/schema contract only; do not treat it as proof of command execution or gameplay progress.

defects.title: Scanner-first StarDock visit purchased 22 cargo holds instead of a scanner
defects.description: Archived telemetry confirms that the ship bought 22 cargo holds at sector 1 during the scanner-acquisition phase. The ship's credits fell from 36,919 to 22,466 while total holds rose from 18 to 40; no Density or Holo Scanner was acquired. This older transaction does not establish the cause of the later one-credit state.
defects.root_cause: The spending transaction is confirmed, but the decision-level cause is not: durable Pilot/Strategic prompt and response records do not show why Cargo Holds were selected instead of the scanner objective or which component initiated the purchase.
affected_components: Autonomous purchase authorization and budget gate
validation_results: The event log records an 18-hold, 36,919-credit baseline, a Cargo Holds prompt with quantity 22, and a subsequent status with 40 holds and 22,466 credits.
The 14,453-credit decrease matches the interval containing the 22-hold purchase; no scanner is recorded in the resulting ship status.
Archived records do not contain the separate later one-credit episode's transaction history, so this event cannot be claimed as its cause.
notes: During the scanner-first objective, authorize only a Density Scanner purchase by default. Do not buy Cargo Holds or other upgrades unless explicitly approved and budget-checked.
After every purchase or trade, require a fresh ship status and compare credits, cargo, holds, and scanner ownership before continuing.

defects.title: WorldTrade script path duplicates the category directory
defects.description: When the configured TWX scripts directory already ended in trading-cashing, loading the approved reference trading-cashing/2-worldtrade.ts appended the category twice and failed with DirectoryNotFoundException.
defects.root_cause: WorldTrade path resolution assumed the configured scripts directory was always the scripts root and did not account for it already being the trading-cashing category directory.
fixes_applied: Resolve the approved WorldTrade reference to an existing absolute path, supporting both the scripts root and the trading-cashing category directory.
validation_results: MTC RPC safety harness passed regression checks for both configured-directory forms.
Release solution build completed with 0 warnings and 0 errors.
After restart, the live log showed script ID 2-WORLDTRADE.TS, the WORLDTRADE menu, and automatic selection of GO! without the duplicate-path compile error.
No completed trade or positive credit delta was observed; WorldTrade earnings remain unverified.
notes: This was an uncounted follow-up after iteration 40, not a completed 15-minute campaign iteration.
The live log ended with the script paused at Command after GO!; successful trading is not established by script loading alone.

defects.title: WorldTrade can issue Holo-only and saved extra commands with a Density Scanner
defects.description: The WorldTrade script loads saved Move~ScanHolo and Move~ExtraSend preferences. Standard holo-scan mode can send `sh` when sector data looks unusual, and the saved f1*ct extra-send macro emits additional keys. With a Density-only scanner, these commands can desynchronize prompts and leave subsequent keys entering the wrong menu.
defects.root_cause: The script trusted persisted navigation settings and did not enforce scanner-compatible scan and movement-command settings before constructing its menu and starting the routine.
fixes_applied: Force Move~ScanHolo to 0 and Move~ExtraSend to an empty string after loading saved preferences and before building the WorldTrade menu.
Keep the changes in the active script instance only; do not overwrite the user's saved navigation preferences.
validation_results: MTC RPC safety and dashboard regression harness passed, including the Density-only scanner policy check.
Release solution build completed with 0 warnings and 0 errors.
The TWX script was not restarted after this source change; actual command sequencing and trading remain pending live verification.
notes: This was an uncounted follow-up after iteration 40, not a completed 15-minute campaign iteration.
Verify that a Density-only WorldTrade run emits no holo-scan or extra-send commands before claiming the defect validated.

known_patterns.name: Stale or inconsistent autopilot prompt telemetry
known_patterns.severity_trend: HIGH; stale heartbeat prompt data again stalled a port-trade quantity response. The timestamp/synthesis race is source-fixed and regression-tested, but live recovery is pending.
known_patterns.recommended_long_term_fix: Preserve empty heartbeat prompts, carry original prompt observation timestamps plus explicit current-prompt confirmation, and correlate the resulting worker event with input acknowledgment and a verified transaction.

known_patterns.name: Scannerless stale-objective movement oscillation
known_patterns.severity_trend: HIGH; iteration 29 again recorded sector transitions 551 to 99 to 551. Iteration 30 moved through sector 206, and iteration 34 again oscillated among 172, 206, and 805 without trade or scanner progress; the exact hold inputs remain unobserved.
known_patterns.recommended_long_term_fix: Keep scanner acquisition deterministic, preserve bounded FedSpace survey/trade phases, and do not treat persistent exploration flags as a scanner substitute for known high-risk sectors.

known_patterns.name: Movement sender rejects echoed destination prompt
known_patterns.severity_trend: MEDIUM; the sender now waits through a MoveSector echo and the MTC RPC harness passes, but the live fix has not yet been exercised.
known_patterns.recommended_long_term_fix: Correlate each destination submission with prompt timestamps and the subsequent Command/sector snapshot; never treat an echoed input prompt as completed movement.

known_patterns.name: Reflex urgency over-classifies routine state changes
known_patterns.severity_trend: HIGH; 16 additional world-observation events fell back after the oneOf schema was deployed; the event UI did not expose the specific validation failure
known_patterns.recommended_long_term_fix: Keep the deterministic gate fail-closed, capture field-specific validation failures, and verify the exact structured output against the live Qwen provider before changing the contract.

known_patterns.name: Stale ship-status refresh at authenticated Command
known_patterns.severity_trend: MEDIUM; RequestShipInformation repeated at sector 551 during the earlier fresh-snapshot run; the action enum now blocks that choice for healthy snapshots, but stale refreshes still need end-to-end verification.
known_patterns.recommended_long_term_fix: Correlate fresh server-prompt events, submitted I/quick-status inputs, RPC acknowledgments, and ship snapshot events; keep command guards fail-closed.

known_patterns.name: Repeated no-transaction port haggle
known_patterns.severity_trend: HIGH; iterations 32-35 again showed incomplete transactions. Iteration 35 verified one recovered 20-unit purchase after three attempts, but the next 876-credit sale quote remained unanswered.
known_patterns.recommended_long_term_fix: Classify trade quote prompts, preserve correlated product/quantity context through recovery, and require a fresh cargo/credit snapshot after every recovered transaction.

known_patterns.name: Ollama inference timeout
known_patterns.severity_trend: MEDIUM; two model roles hit the same 100-second request timeout in one iteration
known_patterns.recommended_long_term_fix: Correlate client timeout events with Ollama queue, model-load, and inference latency telemetry before adjusting timeout or retry behavior.

known_patterns.name: Unbounded model numeric fields
known_patterns.severity_trend: MEDIUM; remediation added, awaiting live verification
known_patterns.recommended_long_term_fix: Mirror deterministic validator bounds in both structured-output schemas and prompts; keep invalid responses visibly failed.

known_patterns.name: Model output contract under-specification
known_patterns.severity_trend: MEDIUM; a live Pilot again selected an action with unmet prerequisites; schema now removes unavailable Dock Shopper actions, live verification pending
known_patterns.recommended_long_term_fix: Define decision-specific field contracts and validate before recording success or applying outcomes.

known_patterns.name: Qwen3 thinking exhausts structured-response budget
known_patterns.severity_trend: HIGH; empty final content recurred at 2048 tokens in iterations 24 and 25 after the original 512-token failure
known_patterns.recommended_long_term_fix: Retain fail-closed parsing and the no-thinking retry; diagnose model-specific thinking/output behavior and verify that a structured final decision is actually produced.

known_patterns.name: Non-movement action paired with a target sector
known_patterns.severity_trend: MEDIUM; five invalid Pilot responses were rejected across iterations 24 and 25, including four in iteration 25
known_patterns.recommended_long_term_fix: Express the relationship between action kind and targetSector in the structured schema where supported, retain parser validation, and test the exact malformed response.

known_patterns.name: Agent readiness lost after reconnect
known_patterns.severity_trend: HIGH; clear-avoids prompt identified and login fix live-validated in iteration 15
known_patterns.recommended_long_term_fix: Persist exact terminal prompt and authentication state transitions; resume only from a recognized safe prompt.

known_patterns.name: Unhandled WebView2 focus exception terminates MTC
known_patterns.severity_trend: HIGH; one fatal occurrence, root cause unconfirmed
known_patterns.recommended_long_term_fix: Identify the invalid WebView2 focus transition and handle that specific lifecycle case without broadly suppressing UI exceptions.

known_patterns.name: Unclassified prompt diagnostics are too coarse
known_patterns.severity_trend: MEDIUM; safe length metadata live-validated in iteration 5
known_patterns.recommended_long_term_fix: Retain privacy-safe prompt metadata and correlate decoder events with authentication state without logging raw terminal content.

known_patterns.name: BBS name prompt parser is too restrictive
known_patterns.severity_trend: HIGH; parser gap corrected, awaiting live verification
known_patterns.recommended_long_term_fix: Keep prompt classification aligned with the actual supported login flow and verify each recognized prompt against a live authenticated transition without exposing raw terminal text.

known_patterns.name: Healthcheck depends on a missing image executable
known_patterns.severity_trend: LOW; corrected and container health validated in iteration 2
known_patterns.recommended_long_term_fix: Verify every container healthcheck command exists in the exact base image and test the recreated container, not only the compose file.

known_patterns.name: Cross-role interaction history crowding
known_patterns.severity_trend: MEDIUM; per-role retention and retrieval implemented, live verification pending
known_patterns.recommended_long_term_fix: Keep retention and retrieval role-scoped end to end; test dashboard role switching while one role produces substantially more events than others.

known_patterns.name: Bounded event queue saturation and prompt loss
known_patterns.severity_trend: HIGH; latest-event preservation and event-noise reduction implemented, live verification pending
known_patterns.recommended_long_term_fix: Measure queue depth, evictions, and event age under load; prioritize freshness and ensure actionable prompts cannot be starved by telemetry.

known_patterns.name: Reactive snapshot backlog
known_patterns.severity_trend: MEDIUM; latest-state coalescing implemented, live verification pending
known_patterns.recommended_long_term_fix: Coalesce superseded state observations before model submission and expose pending/in-flight queue metrics.

known_patterns.name: Agent capability description drift
known_patterns.severity_trend: LOW; description corrected, live verification pending
known_patterns.recommended_long_term_fix: Keep capability metadata aligned with the actual script capability and cover high-impact selection guidance with source-level assertions.

known_patterns.name: Stale queued prompt leaves worker idle
known_patterns.severity_trend: HIGH; iterations 24 and 25 again discarded stale queued prompts without subsequent fresh actions; heartbeat requeue path remains unverified
known_patterns.recommended_long_term_fix: Keep delayed prompts fail-closed while correlating stale events with a fresh authoritative prompt heartbeat; test and instrument the no-new-server-output case.

known_patterns.name: Stale monitor situation shown as healthy
known_patterns.severity_trend: MEDIUM; capture-age warning implemented, live verification pending
known_patterns.recommended_long_term_fix: Expose situation capture age independently from worker heartbeat age and never present an old synchronization status as current.

known_patterns.name: Transient SQLite fixture cleanup locks
known_patterns.severity_trend: LOW; isolated tests and final full-suite reruns pass, root cause unconfirmed
known_patterns.recommended_long_term_fix: Capture fixture disposal failures with exact connection lifetimes and reproduce before changing cleanup or database behavior.

known_patterns.name: Unscanned movement through sector 99 risks ship loss
known_patterns.severity_trend: CRITICAL; iteration 18 confirmed a cruiser-to-Escape-Pod transition at sector 99. Iteration 29 again reached sector 99 and returned to 551; the Release binary predates the new unconditional scanner guard.
known_patterns.recommended_long_term_fix: Require verified Density or Holo Scanner ownership before sector-99 entry, regardless of persistent map exploration flags, and correlate every move decision with terminal acknowledgments and fresh ship status.

known_patterns.name: WorldTrade actions lack scanner and earnings verification
known_patterns.severity_trend: HIGH; WorldTrade-related inputs observed without verified script completion or positive credit delta.
known_patterns.recommended_long_term_fix: Require active-ship Density or Holo Scanner ownership and confirm fresh credits/holds after the WorldTrade routine.

known_patterns.name: Unapproved StarDock hardware purchase consumed scanner funds
known_patterns.severity_trend: HIGH; archived telemetry confirms 14,453 credits spent on 22 Cargo Holds while the scanner objective remained unmet. This is not proven to be the later one-credit loss.
known_patterns.recommended_long_term_fix: During scanner-first operation, whitelist the Density Scanner by default; require an explicit objective and affordability check before any other hardware purchase, then verify the fresh post-purchase status.

known_patterns.name: LLM interaction history is unavailable after shutdown
known_patterns.severity_trend: MEDIUM; model response failure could not be diagnosed from durable prompt/reply evidence.
known_patterns.recommended_long_term_fix: Persist or export redacted prompt and final-response records during the run, before MTC stops.
